notes: Modified cash basis city audit (FYE 9/30/2023). Governmental lines from the Total Governmental Funds column (p5-6); fund balances roll forward (4,473,260 + 2,817,571 - 2,771,357 + 2,055,000 + 378,873 - 124,575 = 6,828,772). Cash and fund balance are separate: ending_cash = cash lines of the governmental funds Balance Sheet (p4), beginning_cash from its 2022 Totals column; fund balances also include LB 840 loans receivable and certificates of deposit, so the cash change does not equal the fund-balance change. Business-type lines from the modified cash proprietary statement (p8-9), which ties to the Statement of Activities (p2: expenditures 5,756,471, charges for services 4,188,125); the accrual-basis proprietary statement (p10-11, report pp43-44, with depreciation and interest expense) is supplementary and not used; the Statement of Cash Flows (p12-13) fills proprietary. Internal service fund (health insurance, net position 175,487) is in governmental activities only on the government-wide statements; its transfers in 69,333 explain the gap between governmental fund transfers (net 254,298) and business-type transfers (-323,631). Bond proceeds of the Sewer fund are printed under nonoperating revenues, so they are a business-type receipt line; the General Fund (Fire) Bond/loan proceeds 2,055,000 are under Other Financing Sources on p6, so debt_proceeds. Statement 'Public Works' 422,377 = Street Fund 392,067 + cemetery 30,310 (categorized streets/highways). Detail: General Fund from the combining schedule by sub-fund (p14; more detailed than the General Fund budget schedule p15-16, which is not recorded); Street and Debt Service Funds from their budget schedules (p17-18; Street 'Charges for services' has budget 1,000 and no actual, not recorded); Sales Tax, Economic Development and Keno Funds from the governmental funds statement columns; utility funds (Light, Water, Sewer, Landfill) from the modified cash proprietary statement columns (no per-fund budget schedules). The All Funds budget schedule (p19-20) is combined and not recorded. Component unit (St. Paul Development Corporation, p21) excluded. Operating grants: Police 2,800, Ambulance 75,000, Library 1,739, grantor not stated. Read pages 1-21 of 21.
